clue.text: Current for TV

definitions.meaning: a river is a flowing current of water, and this is London's river
... Television was the London weekday ITV broadcaster

explanation.walkthrough: THAMES is the river through London; Thames Television held the London weekday ITV licence.
explanation.definitionFit: One name serves both London's great river, a body of flowing water, and the London weekday broadcaster Thames Television.

clue.text: German bard, a male, in Asia

parts.note: he is a male person
E for East, and Asia is the East

explanation.surface: A German poet turns out to be a man living somewhere in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: Heinrich Heine was a German poet; Asia stands for E, the East.
explanation.definitionFit: Heinrich Heine was a celebrated nineteenth-century German poet, and a bard is a poet.

clue.text: He's been gonged

parts.note: gong is British slang for a medal or decoration, so someone gonged has been decorated

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests being struck with a gong, as at a dinner call; 'gong' is British slang for a medal.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a gong is a medal, so a person who has been gonged is a decorated winner.

clue.text: Dry rocky hill that forms part of the front

parts.note: sec is the French word for dry, used of wine
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A dry rocky hill forms part of a front line in some campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a rocky peak on the moors of south-west England; sec is dry wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A military front is divided into sectors, each a section held by one unit.

clue.text: Advance productivity figures are discouraged here

definitions.text: Advance productivity figures are discouraged here

parts.words: Advance productivity figures are discouraged here
parts.note: the proverb says don't count your chickens before they are out of the egg, so early counts of output are frowned upon where eggs are incubated

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a factory memo; it alludes to the proverb about not counting chickens before they emerge from the egg.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where eggs are incubated, where counting chickens in advance of their emerging is proverbially unwise.

clue.text: High school

parts.note: a famous English public school sits on top of a hill north-west of London

explanation.walkthrough: 'High school' suggests the American secondary school; Harrow is a famous English public school on a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: Harrow School, an English public school, stands on a hilltop in the district of that name, so it is literally a school up high.

clue.text: Sad thy ode to the Royal Navy, stirring

definitions.text: Sad thy ode to the Royal Navy, stirring

indicators.note: stirring mixes things up, so the letters before it are jumbled

parts.note: RN is the abbreviation for the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A mournful, stirring poem is addressed to the Royal Navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stirring' rearranges THYODE plus RN; the whole clue also describes a sad ode, a lament.
explanation.definitionFit: A threnody is a lament or dirge, a sad ode for the dead.

clue.text: Painter has no love for composer

indicators.note: having none of something means it is removed from the word

parts.note: Benjamin Robert Haydon was an English history painter
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A painter who lacks a love interest is called a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no' takes the O out of HAYDON. Benjamin Haydon was a nineteenth-century English painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Haydn was the Austrian composer of the Classical period, father of the symphony.

clue.text: Subject of tasteful carving in an Englishman's castle

definitions.text: Subject of tasteful carving in an Englishman's castle

parts.words: Subject of tasteful carving in an Englishman's castle
parts.note: an Englishman's home is his castle, and the Sunday joint carved at the table there is the national dish

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tasteful carving' suggests sculpture in a stately home; it is carving meat. 'An Englishman's home is his castle' is a proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional Sunday joint is carved at an English family table, the home proverbially being a man's castle.

clue.text: Old-clothes-man or old farmer's boy

definitions.meaning: a figure dressed in cast-off clothes stood in a field
a lad once paid to frighten crows off newly sown fields

explanation.walkthrough: 'Old-clothes-man' suggests a rag dealer, but it is the scarecrow in old clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A scarecrow, a dummy in cast-off clothes, keeps crows off crops; in the past a farm boy was also employed for that job.

clue.text: Mundane sun-tour

parts.note: mundane in its root sense means of the world, so this is the world's tour round the sun

explanation.walkthrough: 'Mundane' usually means dull; here it means of the world (Latin mundus).
explanation.definitionFit: The Earth takes one calendar period of twelve months to travel once round the sun.

clue.text: Rich do-gooder ?

definitions.meaning: read as one who does good, the phrase is 'well' plus 'to do'

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a play on words, signalled by the question mark: a do-gooder is someone keen to do well.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means wealthy, and read literally it describes someone whose aim is to do things well, a do-gooder.

clue.text: And more men than these had Sir Richard sick ashore

definitions.text: And more men than these had Sir Richard sick ashore

parts.words: And more men than these had Sir Richard sick ashore
parts.note: a line from Tennyson's poem The Revenge, where Sir Richard Grenville's men lay ill on land

explanation.walkthrough: Tennyson's ballad The Revenge has 'ninety men and more were lying sick ashore' of Grenville's crew.
explanation.definitionFit: In Tennyson's The Revenge, Sir Richard Grenville's crew had that many men and more lying ill on shore at the Azores.

clue.text: Robe in which Cleopatra's maid went into retreat

indicators.note: going into retreat means moving backwards, so the maid's name is read in reverse

parts.note: Iras is one of Cleopatra's attendants in Shakespeare's Antony and Cleopatra

explanation.surface: A robe in which one of Cleopatra's servants withdrew to a retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'went into retreat' reverses IRAS, Cleopatra's attendant in Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: The sari is the draped garment worn by women in India, a kind of robe.

clue.text: Stopping to adjust bracelets? Remarkable !

definitions.meaning: bracelets is slang for handcuffs, so stopping someone to fit them is a police seizure

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bracelets' is old slang for handcuffs.
explanation.definitionFit: Police stopping a suspect put on handcuffs, slangily bracelets; the same word means striking or eye-catching.

clue.text: Grandfather or grandfather clock

definitions.meaning: a long-case clock is an old timekeeper

explanation.definitionFit: A veteran or elderly man is called this, and a grandfather clock is literally an aged timekeeper.

clue.text: Not interested in taking item of bric-a brac to America

parts.note: a curio is an ornamental curiosity, a piece of bric-a-brac
US is the United States

explanation.surface: Someone shows no interest in shipping a knick-knack over to America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' puts US after CURIO; bric-a-brac is assorted small ornaments.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone incurious lacks curiosity, showing no interest.

clue.text: Establishments of service to those seeking to better themselves

definitions.text: Establishments of service to those seeking to better themselves

parts.words: Establishments of service to those seeking to better themselves
parts.note: places where religious services are held help people seeking to improve their souls

explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' suggests an evening-class college; it is a religious service, and the betterment is spiritual.
explanation.definitionFit: Places of worship hold services and help those trying to become better people morally.

clue.text: Ebenezer's clerk in the tank

parts.note: Dickens describes Scrooge's clerk working in a dismal little cell, a sort of tank

explanation.walkthrough: 'The tank' sounds military or like prison slang; Dickens calls the clerk's cell 'a dismal little cell beyond, a sort of tank'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob Cratchit is Ebenezer Scrooge's clerk in A Christmas Carol, kept in a cold cell Dickens calls a sort of tank.

clue.text: Textile strike at hand

definitions.meaning: the fabric band at the end of a sleeve, by the wrist
to slap with the open hand

explanation.definitionFit: The fabric band at a sleeve's end is the textile sense, and a slap with the hand is the other.

clue.text: Tar was wont to be given a bad name

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, and tar both mean a sailor
used, as in 'used to', means was accustomed

explanation.surface: A sailor was accustomed to being slandered.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'Tar', which OCR read as 'Car'. Both tar and AB are crossword words for a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: To abuse someone can mean to revile or malign them, giving them a bad reputation.

clue.text: The least disinterested' of financiers

parts.note: disinterested means impartial, but here it is read as having no interest, so this lender charges the most interest

explanation.walkthrough: 'Disinterested' means impartial, but the clue reads it as not charging interest.
explanation.definitionFit: A moneylender charging excessive interest is the most interested in interest of all lenders.

clue.text: More husbandly binder

parts.note: a binder using cord on the farm, and 'more husbandly' looks like a comparative adjective

explanation.walkthrough: 'More husbandly' looks like a comparative adjective; the answer is a noun for one who binds with cord, as in husbandry, farming.
explanation.definitionFit: One who ties with cord is a binder; the clue dresses the word as a comparative, like 'ropier', of farming husbandry.

clue.text: Bed-maker otherwise prepared to do a bunk ?

indicators.note: otherwise means in another way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A college bed-maker is otherwise getting ready to run off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'otherwise' rearranges BEDMAKER. 'Do a bunk' is British slang for run away, but here it means use a ship's bunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Having gone aboard ship, a passenger is ready to sleep in a berth, a bunk.

clue.text: Jug-jug

parts.note: 'jug-jug' is the nightingale's song, but read as one vessel plus another it is a pair of pitchers

explanation.walkthrough: 'Jug-jug' is a traditional rendering of the nightingale's song; read literally it is two jugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitchers for water are vessels of this kind, so a jug and a jug make a plural of them.

clue.text: Halt, in need of a stiffener ?

explanation.walkthrough: 'Halt' here is the old adjective for lame, not stop.
explanation.definitionFit: Halt means lame, walking with an uneven gait; something floppy needs stiffening.

clue.text: Nature's hard greetings ?

parts.note: greetings are hails, and nature's hard ones are frozen pellets falling from the sky

explanation.walkthrough: To hail is to greet; the question mark signals the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Pellets of ice falling in a storm; a greeting is a hail, so they are nature's hard hails.

clue.text: Lady G. sir, worried about the ash

indicators.note: worried means shaken about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Lady G tells a gentleman she is anxious about ash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' rearranges LADYGSIR; 'about' links.
explanation.definitionFit: In Norse myth the world tree is an enormous ash binding heaven, earth and the underworld.

clue.text: Stop and see the godly about a point

indicators.note: about means around, so the godly ones surround the point

parts.note: a deist believes in God, so is one of the godly
S, south, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Stop and visit the pious about a matter in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts S inside DEIST.
explanation.definitionFit: To cease or leave off doing something is to stop.
